question: Which customer statements support that conclusion, and how many calls is it based on?

answer.answer_markdown:
**The conclusion rests on 407 individual customer contacts - 7.5% of the 5,425 in the index - and every one of them can be opened and read.**

The path from the claim to the evidence is short. The pipeline read each contact, extracted the issue in the customer's own words, and grouped those wordings into themes. "Unexplained account closures or restrictions" is the largest of them at 407 calls, ahead of the next theme at 396. Those 407 are not one story counted many times: they carry 417 distinct issue wordings across 7 products, so the number is 407 different people describing the same experience.

The statements below are the customer side of that group, pulled verbatim from the contacts themselves. They run from August 2024 to June 2026 and cover checking and savings, credit cards, mortgages, auto loans, transfers and debt collection - the same complaint in six different places, not an artefact of one product or one bad month.

It concentrates where the money sits: 275 of the 407 are checking or savings contacts, which is 12.8% of all checking and savings traffic against 7.5% overall, a lift of 1.71. And it is steady rather than a spike - the theme shows up in every month the index covers, with its heaviest month at 29 calls in November 2025.

One honest note on provenance: 404 of the 407 are written complaints, and only 3 come from the synthetic phone-conversation set. So these are customers' written words, not call transcripts.

quotes.quote: I have never committed fraud or any illegal activity on these accounts or any money laundering. I asked for a reason and they wouldn't tell me anything. They just closed the accounts.
quotes.why: June 2026, checking/savings: the complaint the theme is named for - closure with no reason given.

quotes.quote: Chase refused to give me that information.
quotes.why: August 2024, auto loan: the oldest end of the range, same refusal to explain.

quotes.quote: I called Chase customer service and was informed that my account had been closed without prior notification.
quotes.why: March 2026, checking/savings: closure discovered only after the fact, no notice.

quotes.quote: In this call, I passed the security review, yet I was given a reason that my fund was insufficient. My wire was hence cancelled.
quotes.why: January 2025, transfers: a restriction applied after the customer passed the security review.

quotes.quote: my agreed upon payment would not be accepted because of potential fraud and equity theft
quotes.why: September 2025, mortgage: a payment blocked as suspected fraud.

quotes.quote: When my mother sent a XXXX payment from her account to mine for $3000.00 that she owed me prior they sent an email the very same day stating my checking account and chase prime cards were all being terminated
quotes.why: May 2026, credit card: closure triggered same-day by an incoming family payment.

quotes.quote: I was told the accounts could not be reopened because they believed the caller had properly verified my identity.
quotes.why: July 2025, debt collection: accounts kept closed on the bank's own verification judgement.

quotes.quote: Chase refused to put the time and date of the account closure.
quotes.why: April 2026, checking/savings: the bank refusing to document the closure.

caveats: The index holds two corpora: 4,425 real written complaints about one bank (July 2024 to June 2026) and 1,000 synthetic agent/customer phone conversations (September 2023 only). The 407 figure covers both.
For this theme the mix is lopsided: 404 of the 407 contacts are written complaints and 3 are synthetic conversations, so the quoted statements are almost entirely written, not spoken.
These are complaints to a regulator, not a sample of all customers. They say what the unhappy minority experienced, not how common the experience is across the customer base.
The customer states that the bank gave no explanation. The index records what the customer said, not whether the bank in fact had a valid reason it was not permitted to disclose.

sql.sql: SELECT * FROM themes WHERE theme_id = ?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1
SELECT tc.call_id, c.date, c.week, c.month, c.region FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE tc.theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY c.date

SELECT t.driver_category, COUNT(DISTINCT t.call_id) AS n FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 GROUP BY t.driver_category ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT t.driver, t.call_id FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1
SELECT w.rank, w.issue_statement, w.call_id, w.date, w.product FROM theme_wordings w JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = w.call_id WHERE w.theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY w.rank LIMIT 12
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.week AS period, COUNT(*) AS n FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
SELECT c.week AS period, c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY period, c.call_id

SELECT m.from_theme, f.name AS from_name, m.into_theme, m.pass, m.reason, m.judged_by, m.created_at FROM theme_merges m JOIN themes f ON f.theme_id = m.from_theme WHERE m.into_theme = ? OR f.effective_theme_id = ? ORDER BY m.created_at, m.from_theme
SELECT * FROM emerging_scores WHERE entity_type = 'theme' AND entity_id = ? AND as_of_week = ?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY n_calls DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
